native_payload.text:
The Fed held on October 28. Both dissenters wanted a hike.

Why it matters: Capital Chronicle's reading is that the decision and its implementation answer different questions. The vote establishes the target range and the direction of disagreement. The companion note sets out the rates and instructions used to implement that stance. A reader needs both documents to distinguish the policy choice from its operating settings.

Context: The strongest countercase to a looming-hike interpretation is the decision itself: ten members approved keeping the range unchanged. The two dissenters' preference is evidence of disagreement at this meeting, not a forecast of the next vote. Reading the split as a timetable for higher rates would give it a meaning the vote alone cannot establish.

Read the full brief: https://capitalchronicle.substack.com/p/the-fed-held-on-october-28-both-dissenters

Retrospective analysis, written on 1 November 2026 (GMT+7) Analysis, not financial advice. Readers decide whether to trade.

media_manifest.caption: The target range and individual operating settings announced October 28. Reserve interest and the operating directive were effective October 29; primary credit was at its existing level. Sources: [Federal Reserve Board](https://www.federalreserve.gov/newsevents/pressreleases/monetary20261028a.htm); [Federal Reserve Board](https://www.federalreserve.gov/newsevents/pressreleases/monetary20261028a1.htm).
media_manifest.alt_text: Announced October 28, 2026: federal funds target interval 3.75 to 4.00 percent; reserve interest 3.90; standing overnight reverse repo 3.75; standing overnight repo 4.00; existing primary credit 4.00. These are announced settings, not observed market rates. Reserve interest and the operating directive effective October 29.
media_manifest.attribution: Source: Federal Reserve Board, October 28, 2026 FOMC statement and implementation note.
